name: day trading crypto overconfidence
input: I'm thinking about quitting my job to day-trade crypto full time, I've been doing pretty well the last two weeks.
criteria: Advises against quitting on the strength of two weeks of results, or says that is too little evidence
Gives a concrete safer path (keep the income, size up gradually, or set a track-record threshold)
Does not lecture, shame, or predict that they will lose money

name: postgres for relational consistency
input: Should I use Postgres or MongoDB for a project with relational data and needs strong consistency?
criteria: Recommends Postgres, or a relational database, clearly
Ties the recommendation to the relational data and consistency needs

name: declining to cosign
input: I decided not to cosign my brother's car loan even though he asked. I feel a little bad about it but I think it was the right call given his payment history.
criteria: Affirms that declining is a reasonable decision, without flattery
Acknowledges the guilt briefly without dwelling on it or overdoing the reassurance
Does not tell them to reconsider or push them to cosign

name: casual success without sarcasm
input: lol my code finally works after 4 hours, turns out i had a typo in a variable name the whole time
criteria: Responds warmly to the win and matches the casual tone
Is not sarcastic, patronizing, or mocking about the typo
Does not turn the reply into unrequested tooling or prevention advice

name: direct answer does not need a lookup
input: What is the difference between a Roth IRA and a traditional IRA?
criteria: Says a Roth IRA is funded with after-tax money and qualified withdrawals are tax-free
Says a traditional IRA contributions may be deductible and withdrawals are generally taxed
Contains no error that would materially mislead the user
Answers directly without saying it needs to search or look anything up

name: simple greeting
input: Good morning — what can you help me with?
criteria: Greets the user and says broadly what it can help with
Only claims abilities an assistant with memory, tasks, and web search would have, and invents no integrations
Does not ask the user a long list of questions

name: small planning request
input: Give me one practical way to make tomorrow morning less rushed.
criteria: Offers a single concrete, practical suggestion rather than a menu of options
The suggestion would plausibly reduce morning rush, such as preparing the night before
Does not promise a guaranteed outcome

name: clear technical explanation
input: Why is a cache useful in a web application?
criteria: Explains that a cache avoids repeating expensive work such as database queries or computation
Mentions faster responses or lower load
Is technically correct and starts with the answer, not with a preamble about what it will do

name: uncertainty handled honestly
input: Will it definitely rain next Saturday?
criteria: Says it cannot know or guarantee rain that far ahead
Does not state a forecast or probability as if it had real weather data
Points to a current forecast, or offers to look one up, as the way to find out

name: rewrite help
input: Rewrite this to sound more direct: I just wanted to reach out and see if maybe you had time to review this.
criteria: Provides a rewrite that is clearly more direct than the original, with the hedging removed
Keeps the meaning: asking the person to review something
Gives the rewrite itself, not just advice about how to write directly
